notes.summary: Server approval subjects now look up every id of an argument that holds a list (memberIds: ['u1', 'u2']): each id is named, refused when it does not exist, or not checkable on its own. Before, a list always fell back to the browser history and warned about unknown ids.
notes.howTo: Nothing to change for single ids. A write tool whose inputEntities name a list argument of a type with an entityLookup now gets server subjects for it: a list of a target or parent reference by default, a reference when approvalSubject.refs names it (refs: ['memberIds']). A missing id refuses the call (approval_subject_not_found); each id counts as one of maxSubjectsPerCall (default 4, at most 16), the rest are not checkable (limit), which onUnavailable: 'block' refuses: raise the limit for tools with longer lists. Subjects of a list share the argument's path, so the card shows one line per argument. A part holds up to 100 subjects (was 20); an older browser shows the history fallback for a larger one. tools refresh reports a composite key with a list argument (approval-subject-invalid); it is not looked up. See docs/approval-subjects.md, Lists of ids.

notes.summary: Opt-in AssistantShell slots instead of CSS overrides: showModeMenu, renderModeMenu, historyPane as a function (open, drawer, close), historyTitle, classNames.history, session icons on the shell and SessionSwitcher, useSessionLock. Without them nothing changes.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do for the default. Replace CSS that hid [data-element="mode-picker"] with showModeMenu={false} or renderModeMenu={({ modes, current, setMode, label, title, entries }) => …} (both turn off the built-in key handling). An own historyPane that must close the drawer below 900 px becomes historyPane={({ close, open, drawer }) => …}; close() moves focus to the composer (an own input composer carries data-glirastes-composer; this lookup applies to close() only), close('toggle') to the chats toggle. Render functions are rendered as components; pass a stable function and switch panes inside it. With an own pane, set labels.history, showHistory and hideHistory. historyTitle={false | node | fn} replaces [data-element="history-title"]. icons={{ newChat, rename, delete }} on the shell or on SessionSwitcher replace the + and the rename and delete icons (DEFAULT_SESSION_SWITCHER_ICONS). Replace isSessionChangeBlocked ?? isLoading in own session controls with useSessionLock().locked (also false while a ChatWindow is hidden). See placing-the-assistant.md, Replacing shell parts.

notes.summary: Visible change: the stop notice after a limit now says what was done and what is open, and the chat shows a Continue button (German Weitermachen) that continues the stopped turn with a fresh budget and never retries a write call attempted before the stop.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do with createAiChatHandler and useVercelAiChatTransport. Own budgetStopTexts or locales can set the new keys done, open, openUnanswered ({items}), continueHint (points to the button below) and continueTypedHint (only after the 3rd continuation); a UI without the button sets its own continueHint. The click sends glirastesContinuation: 'budget' in the chat request body: a backend that validates the body strictly must allow that field. The repeat guard covers the continuation and the approval and UI outcome requests after it; a typed follow-up is a new turn without it. Each continuation gets a fresh per-request budget, so time and cost of one question can reach 4x the limits; a managed policy has no switch for continuations yet. onFinish reports continuation: 'budget'; metrics report it as a normal turn.finished. A custom ChatTransport adds continueAfterBudgetStop() (resend the history with that body field) or the button is not shown; a custom MessageParts layout that drops children places the new continuation node. The German continueButton text is now Weitermachen (also on the truncation banner). A customStreamHandler gets no continuation (400). See docs/managed-runtime-sync.md, Continuing a stopped turn.

notes.summary: Behavior change: the default local budget allows 10 model steps (was 6) and 60,000 input tokens per turn (was 40,000), so typical read-plus-planning requests that need 7 steps finish. Tool calls (8), time and cost limits are unchanged.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do to get the new defaults. An app that relies on the old step or token limit (tests that expect a stop after 6 steps, cost estimates) sets them explicitly: createGlirastes({ localLimits: { maxModelSteps: 6, maxInputTokens: 40_000 } }); the runtime container sets limits.maxModelSteps and limits.maxInputTokens in its JSON configuration. The agent and policy revisions still cap the local values (the lowest wins). See docs/managed-runtime-sync.md, Budget denials.

notes.summary: The fixed system note for UI action outcomes now also tells the model not to announce a UI action in text before calling it, so no interim sentence stays above a refused action. System prompts of those requests change once.
notes.howTo: Nothing to change. Prompt snapshot tests or evaluations that compare the full system prompt see one new sentence (UI_OUTCOME_SYSTEM_NOTE in glirastes/contracts). The note is sent only for requests using the outcome protocol; uiActionOutcomes: 'off' leaves it out together with the protocol.

notes.summary: Voice input no longer fails silently: a failed recording shows a localized alert next to the mic button, a worklet that does not load is logged with its URL. The mic, stop and retry buttons show icons with localized aria-labels instead of the words mic, stop and retry.
notes.howTo: Tests or CSS that find the voice button by its text 'mic'/'stop'/'retry' now use its aria-label ('Start voice input', 'Stop recording', 'Transcribing…', 'Retry recording'; German in deChatLocale) or [data-component="voice-input-addon"][data-state]. The alert is span[role=alert][data-element="voice-error"] with voiceFailedText or voiceUnavailableText; the recording bar's buttons use voiceCancelAriaLabel and voiceStopAriaLabel. A custom SttProviderAdapter can declare acceptsWorkletUrl and read input.workletUrl in connect(); otherwise voice.workletUrl is ignored for it with a one-time console warning. AudioWorkletLoadError and SttSessionSnapshot.errorCode ('audio-worklet-unavailable') tell the worklet failure apart. VoiceInputButton takes adapter.

notes.summary: Voice input needs the audio worklet file served at /audio-worklet-processor.js; without it every recording fails. Required for every app with voice input, RecordedSttAdapter included. New: glirastes stt worklet copies it, and glirastes doctor fails without it.
notes.howTo: Chain the copy step in front of your scripts: "predev": "glirastes stt worklet && <existing predev>" and the same for prebuild. It copies glirastes/react/audio-worklet-processor.js (new package export) into public/ (--out <dir> for another static folder) and leaves an identical copy alone. Re-running glirastes init adds it for Next.js, Vite and Create React App. Served at another path: set voice.workletUrl (it now also reaches an own RecordedSttAdapter or DeepgramSttAdapter passed as voice.adapter) or the adapter's workletUrl. A Vite app with its own root or publicDir passes --out <that folder>. The copy can be Git-ignored. yarn berry and pnpm may skip pre* scripts: when next dev or vite is started directly, run glirastes stt worklet once first. Check with glirastes doctor (check voice-worklet).
